digest.component_or_area: Error reporting across MCP, CLI, and library interfaces
propositions: MCP currently returns unstructured error prose or ad-hoc partial shapes instead of the structured error_envelope discriminator that the CLI emits, preventing agents from reliably distinguishing error types across interfaces.

The CLI, library, and MCP interfaces emit error codes from different, uncentralized sources with no single vocabulary or classifier, allowing codes to exist on only one interface and breaking the three-way cross-interface agreement contract.

TicketNotFoundError must be a distinct subclass raised only at genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313) so error_code_for can classify by isinstance rather than message substring, making error codes message-independent and stable per AC4.
The read facade flattens TicketNotFoundError to a generic RebarError, so the error_code must be attached as an attribute on the raised RebarError and checked by the classifier before fallback.

MCP tool failures must raise McpEnvelopeError carrying a structured .envelope dict (built via error_envelope with a vocabulary code from error_code_for) so the guard delivers consistent discriminators without dropping agent-signal fields like resolution_class or kind.

The error_envelope.required schema constraint must be relaxed to exclude input so target-less MCP failures (gate refusals not tied to a ticket) are valid, while CLI envelopes with input remain unchanged.
